Write the Survival Analysis Report to a Word Document

Source: R/write_survival_report.R
write_survival_report.Rd

Writes a Word report on the extrapolation of survival data for health technology assessment (the standard parametric models of NICE DSU TSD 14 and spline-based models), with print-ready names of the models:

  1. Overview: data, outcome, arms, time unit, reporting interval and the variables of the hazard ratios. Items not given are left as placeholders in square brackets.

  2. Methods: Kaplan-Meier analysis, hazard ratios, diagnostics (with a table of the shapes of the hazard functions), standard parametric models, spline-based extrapolation and software versions.

  3. Results: data summary, Kaplan-Meier curves (all arms and each arm) and tables, hazard ratios, smoothed empirical hazards, distribution diagnostics, proportional hazards assessment (Schoenfeld residuals, Grambsch-Therneau test, QQ plot), and for each arm and for both arms fitted together: the standard parametric models (overlaid plots, AIC and BIC, and hazard and survival plots of each model) and the spline models (placement of the knots, fit statistics, median, mean and predicted survival at the landmark times, and overlaid plots).

The figures are drawn as PNG files and embedded in the document; the versions without and with confidence intervals are both included by default, so that they do not have to be recomputed. The tables of fit statistics and predicted survival of the spline models of both arms are given for each arm, so that they fit the page.

Usage

write_survival_report(
  x,
  file,
  data_label = NULL,
  outcome = NULL,
  author = NULL,
  version = NULL,
  interval = NULL,
  landmarks = NULL,
  time_horizon = NULL,
  hazard_ratios = NULL,
  conf_int = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  n_sim = 1000,
  seed = 1,
  template = NULL,
  dpi = 300
)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

file

Path of the .docx file to write (replaced if it exists).

data_label, outcome, author, version

NULL or a string: the data (trial, data cut-off, population), the outcome (for example "Overall survival"), the author and the version of the report.

interval

Spacing of the reporting times of the Kaplan-Meier tables. The default NULL uses the spacing of the time axis of the plots of the data (for example 12 months).

landmarks

Times of the predicted survival of the spline models. The default NULL uses 6 months and 1, 2, 5 and 10 years, in the time unit of the data.

time_horizon

Time to which the models are extrapolated in the plots. The default NULL uses the last landmark time.

hazard_ratios

Data frame returned by estimate_hazard_ratio (for example with the covariates and strata chosen for the analysis). The default NULL uses the Cox model of the arm without adjustment.

conf_int

Logical vector: the versions of the figures without (FALSE) and with (TRUE) confidence intervals; both by default.

n_sim, seed

Number of simulations and seed of the confidence intervals of the models (see predict_survival).

template

NULL or the path of a .docx file whose page set-up and styles are used (for example an empty document with the styles of the organisation). The default NULL uses the template of the package: A4 page, Arial 10 pt, numbered headings in dark red, bold captions, and tables with a dark red header row (made by inst/templates/make_report_template.py). The styles "Title", "Subtitle", "heading 1" to "heading 4", "Caption", "Table Caption", "Figure", "Table Text" and the table style "Report Table" are used when the document defines them.

dpi

Resolution of the figures. The default is 300.

Value

The path file, invisibly.

Examples

# \donttest{
dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = NULL,
                            fit_type = "independent")
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".docx")
write_survival_report(fits, path, outcome = "Overall survival",
                      conf_int = FALSE, dpi = 100)
unlink(path)
# }
